title: Mechanical Control: Cams, Cranks and Ratchets
summary: Types of motion, cams and followers, cranks and sliders, ratchet and pawl, and combining mechanisms in systems, including pulley systems with mechanical advantage.

rows: Rotary
Turning in a circle
A wheel, a fan
Linear
Moving in a straight line in one direction
A train on a straight track, a conveyor belt
Reciprocating
Moving backwards and forwards in a straight line
A piston in an engine, a saw
Oscillating
Swinging backwards and forwards in an arc
A pendulum, a swing, windscreen wipers

notes.text: Mechanisms are used to **change one type of motion into another** and to **control** movement.

notes.text: A **cam** is a specially shaped piece fixed to a rotating shaft. As it turns, a **follower** resting on it moves up and down. The cam changes **rotary** motion into **reciprocating** motion.

rows: Pear (egg)-shaped cam
Stays still for most of the turn (dwell), then rises and falls once
Circular cam with an off-centre shaft (eccentric)
Rises and falls smoothly and continuously
Snail (drop) cam
Rises slowly, then drops suddenly; turns in one direction only
Heart-shaped cam
Rises and falls at a steady, uniform speed

notes.text: Cams are used in car engines (to open and close valves), sewing machines and moving toys (automata).

notes.title: How far does the follower rise?
notes.problem: A pear-shaped cam has a longest radius of 40 mm and a shortest radius of 25 mm. How far does the follower rise and fall?
steps: The follower is lowest when it rests on the shortest radius.
It is highest at the longest radius.

notes.text: A **crank** is an arm attached to a rotating shaft. Joined to a **connecting rod** and a **slider** (piston), it changes **rotary** motion into **reciprocating** motion, or the other way round. In a car engine, the pistons move up and down, and the crankshaft changes this into rotary motion that turns the wheels.

notes.text: A **ratchet** is a gear wheel with sloping teeth, and a **pawl** is a small lever that drops into the teeth. The ratchet can turn in **one direction only**; the pawl stops it from slipping back. Uses: winches, fishing reels, cable ties, clock springs, ratchet spanners and the mechanism that holds a car's handbrake.

notes.text: Many machines combine mechanisms. A bicycle uses levers (pedals and brake levers), a chain and sprockets, a ratchet (freewheel) and a cable-operated brake (bell crank).
